classification.difficultyReason: Identifies similar right triangles in a mirror situation and pairs their corresponding heights and ground distances.

content.prompt: Amina would like to determine the height of a tree. A mirror is placed on the ground 1 m from her feet. The mirror is 3 m from the base of the tree. Amina’s eyes are 1.5 m above the ground. Given Amina can see the top of the tree in the mirror, determine the height $h$ m of the tree.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13, mirror and tree diagram in the left column
spec.description: Native mathematical line diagram preserves the eye-height vertical, mirror junction, tree-height vertical, ground distances, sight lines and right-angle marks. Decorative green ground and tree silhouette are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The mirror is between Amina and the tree. Ground distances are 1 m and 3 m; eye height is 1.5 m; tree height is h m. No numerical tree height is printed in the question figure.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements and the unknown h are visible.

answer.worked:
The two triangles are right-angled. Their angles at the mirror are equal by reflection, so they are similar by AAA.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{h}{1.5}&=\frac{3}{1}\\h&=1.5\times3\\h&=4.5\,\mathrm{m}.\end{align*}$$
